unit.title: Attend to breakdown in hazardous area

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: In electrical work, what makes a place a 'hazardous area'?
options: It has machines with moving parts that could trap or crush a worker
A flammable gas, vapour, mist or dust may be present in the air
It has cables that run at more than 220 V
It is outdoors and open to rain and lightning

questions.stem: Which three things must be present together for a fire or an explosion?
options: Fuel, oxygen and a source of ignition
Fuel, water vapour and a source of ignition
Oxygen, nitrogen and heat
Fuel, oxygen and carbon dioxide

questions.stem: Which workplace in Jamaica is most likely to have areas classified as hazardous because of flammable vapour?
options: A school classroom block
A furniture showroom
A distillery's spirit store
A hotel laundry with large dryers

questions.stem: Which of these places may be classified as hazardous because of a combustible dust?
options: A car wash bay with high-pressure water jets
A sugar factory's bagging area
A town water storage tank on a hill
A cold room used for storing fresh fish

questions.stem: In the zone system for gases, which zone is a place where an explosive gas atmosphere is present all the time or for long periods?
options: Zone 0
Zone 1
Zone 2
Zone 20

questions.stem: An explosive gas atmosphere is likely to occur now and then during normal operation. Which zone is this?
options: Zone 0
Zone 1
Zone 2
Zone 22

questions.stem: Which zone is a place where an explosive gas atmosphere is not likely in normal operation and, if it does occur, lasts only a short time?
options: Zone 0
Zone 1
Zone 21
Zone 2

questions.stem: Where do you find out which zone applies at the spot where a broken light fitting must be replaced?
options: On the area classification drawing for the site
From the most experienced operator on the night shift
From the colour of the cable sheaths in that area
From how strong the smell of fuel is in the air

questions.stem: Zones 20, 21 and 22 are used for which kind of hazard?
options: Flammable gases and vapours
Combustible dusts
Toxic gases
Radiation sources

questions.stem: Some sites, often those built to North American codes, mark their hazardous areas in a different way. What do they use instead of zones?
options: Colour bands and numbers
Classes and divisions
Grades and stages
Floors and levels

questions.stem: What does the 'Ex' marking on a piece of electrical equipment tell you?
options: It is an export model fitted with a foreign plug and cord
It is extra-low voltage equipment that cannot cause a spark
It is certified for hazardous areas named in its marking
It was taken out of service and is waiting for a repair

questions.stem: Why does the marking on an Ex light fitting include a temperature class, such as T3 or T4?
options: It shows the lowest air temperature the fitting can work in
It shows how much the lamp warms the room around it
It shows the temperature at which the fitting was rain-tested
It shows the highest surface temperature the fitting can reach

questions.stem: The area classification says the gas present needs equipment of temperature class T3 or better. Which fitting may be used?
options: A fitting marked T1
A fitting marked T2
A fitting marked T4
Any fitting with no T class

questions.stem: Gas group IIC equipment is suitable for the most easily ignited gases, such as hydrogen. Where else may it be used?
options: Only where hydrogen is present, nowhere else
Where IIA or IIB equipment is required too
Only in dust zones 20, 21 and 22
Only outdoors, away from buildings

questions.stem: How does a flameproof (Ex d) enclosure protect against an explosion?
options: It is sealed so tightly that gas can never get inside it
It keeps the circuit energy so low that no spark can ever light the gas
It is kept full of clean air at a pressure above the room's
It contains an inside explosion and cools gases leaving its joints

questions.stem: What is the idea behind intrinsic safety (Ex i)?
options: Contain any explosion inside a strong, heavy cast-metal box
Fill the enclosure with sand or oil to keep gas out
Limit the energy in the circuit so it cannot ignite the gas
Keep the equipment inside a pressurised room

questions.stem: Increased safety (Ex e) equipment, such as some terminal boxes, mainly protects by:
options: containing an explosion inside a strong cast casing
stopping arcs, sparks and hot spots by careful design
limiting circuit energy below the level that ignites gas
purging the box with clean air before it is switched on

questions.stem: A pump motor in a Zone 1 area at a fuel depot has stopped. Who may open its terminal box?
options: Only an authorised person working under a permit
Any qualified electrician who happens to be on site that day
The pump operator, as long as the motor is cool
A trainee, as long as a supervisor is somewhere on site

questions.stem: Which item is normally part of a permit to work for electrical work in a hazardous area?
options: The prices of the spare parts and who will pay for them
The home addresses and phone numbers of the workers
Gas test results and the isolations in place
The weather forecast for the week ahead at the site

questions.stem: Before work starts on a breakdown in a hazardous area, why is the air tested with a gas detector?
options: To find out which product is flowing through the pump line today
To measure the air temperature for the job record
To check the humidity before cable joints are made
To prove the gas level is safe before and during the work

questions.stem: A gas detector shows 10% LEL near a fuel pump. What does this reading mean?
options: The gas is at one tenth of the lowest level that can burn
The air holds ten times the gas needed for it to burn
Ten per cent of the air in the area has been replaced by gas
The detector's battery has only ten per cent of its charge left

questions.stem: Why is a portable gas detector bump-tested before use each day?
options: To charge its battery fully for a long shift
To set its clock to the right date and time
To blow dust out of its sensor and its filter
To prove its sensors and alarm respond to gas

questions.stem: A flameproof motor starter has been isolated and locked off. What must you do before opening its cover?
options: Wait for the time on its warning label before opening
Open it at once, so the fault can be seen while it is warm
Spray water over it so it cools down more quickly
Loosen the cover bolts by tapping them with a hammer

questions.stem: A breakdown on a pump motor in a hazardous area needs electrical isolation. What else may the permit require?
options: A fresh coat of paint on the motor housing first
Removal of the warning signs from the area
Switching on every light fitting in the area
Process isolation of the pump as well

questions.stem: In a hazardous area, how should a circuit be proved dead?
options: With a tester allowed by the permit, checked before and after use
By touching the conductors quickly with the back of the hand
By looking to see whether the pilot light is off
By shorting the conductors with a screwdriver to see if it sparks

questions.stem: A light fitting in a Zone 2 area at a fuel station has failed. What should be your first step?
options: Fit any spare light fitting the store has in stock
Take off the glass cover to look at the lamp
Report it and arrange a permit before any work
Link out the fitting so the other lights work

questions.stem: A failed Ex motor must be replaced. What must the new motor match?
options: Only its power in kilowatts and its shaft speed
Only its frame size, colour and mounting holes
Only the price the purchasing officer agreed
Its protection type, gas group and temperature class

questions.stem: Why must you NOT drill an extra cable entry hole in a flameproof enclosure on site?
options: It would add too much weight to the enclosure
It voids the certificate and may weaken the box
It lets light from the lamp shine out of the side wall
It will spoil the paint and make the box rust

questions.stem: During a repair, the machined faces (flamepath) of a flameproof cover are found scratched and pitted. What should be done?
options: Keep it out of service and replace the part as the maker says
File the faces smooth with a flat file and refit the cover
Fill the scratches with silicone sealant, let it set, and refit it
Add a rubber gasket between the faces to close the gap

questions.stem: When closing a flameproof enclosure after a repair, which is correct?
options: Fit half of the bolts, so long as each one is tightened very hard
Use any bolts of the same size from the toolbox
Paint over the joint all round to keep the rain out
Fit every bolt, of the right type, tightened as the maker says

questions.stem: A cable gland on an Ex enclosure has to be replaced. Which gland is correct?
options: Any plastic gland that fits the hole and grips the cable
A standard brass gland like those used in ordinary wiring
A certified gland suited to the enclosure and the cable
The cheapest gland in the store with the right thread size

questions.stem: After a repair, one cable entry in an Ex enclosure is no longer used. How should it be closed?
options: With PVC tape wrapped tightly over the hole
With a certified stopping plug of the right type
With a wooden plug cut to fit the thread
Left open, so that the heat inside the box can escape freely

questions.stem: Why must intrinsically safe (IS) circuits be kept apart from ordinary power circuits?
options: So the IS cables can be painted a different colour
So that the cables are easier to count at the yearly inspection
So the IS signals travel faster along the cable
So a fault cannot push extra energy into the IS circuit

questions.stem: An insulation resistance test is planned on cables in a hazardous area. What must be in place first?
options: A permit that allows the test, with a gas test done first
Nothing extra, because an insulation tester uses only DC
Only a fire extinguisher close to the test position
Only a second person to hold the test leads

questions.stem: Why are workers in some hazardous areas asked to wear antistatic footwear?
options: To keep their feet dry when the floor is wet
To stop them slipping on spilt oil and fuel
To stop static charge building up and making a spark
To protect their toes from heavy tools that are dropped on them

questions.stem: Why must ordinary mobile phones and torches be left outside a classified area unless they are certified for it?
options: They might be dropped and lost in the drains or pipe trenches
They distract the workers from the permit's rules
They can make a spark or hot spot that lights the gas
Their batteries do not last long in the hot sun

questions.stem: An Ex motor at a sewage pumping station keeps tripping. Inspection shows water inside its terminal box. What is the most likely cause?
options: A damaged gland or cover seal
The motor is too small for the pump
The supply frequency is 50 Hz
The pump is running too slowly

questions.stem: A motor in a hazardous area has tripped its protection. What should you NOT do?
options: Find out the cause of the trip before resetting
Keep resetting it so that the pump keeps running
Report the trip to the person in charge of the plant
Check the motor and its cable under a permit

questions.stem: After a breakdown repair on Ex equipment, what must happen before it goes back into service?
options: It must be painted bright yellow so people know it was repaired
It must stay switched off for a week while the seals settle
Nothing more, as long as it works when it is switched on
A recorded inspection of the Ex features by a competent person

questions.stem: Why is the hazardous area equipment register (or dossier) updated after a part is replaced?
options: So the store can send the bill to the right client
So the old area drawing can be thrown away
So it shows what is now fitted and its certificate
So the next repair can be done without a permit

questions.stem: During a repair at a fuel depot, the gas detector alarms. What should the team do?
options: Switch every light off quickly so they cannot make a spark
Finish the job quickly before the gas spreads any further
Stop work and leave by the agreed route, as the site plan says
Turn the detector off and carry on, as it often gives false alarms

questions.stem: A breakdown repair needs a bracket to be welded in a hazardous area. What is needed besides the normal permit?
options: A spare pair of welding gloves and a second helmet
A larger welding set so the job finishes sooner
A written note to the client's accounts department
A hot work permit and a gas test before and during

questions.stem: You lead a team of three on a breakdown at an LPG bottling plant. One worker has not been trained for hazardous areas. What should you do?
options: Let him do the repair while you watch him from the gate
Send him home for the day without any pay
Keep him outside the classified area and brief him
Let him work inside if he promises to be careful

questions.stem: Which item belongs in the breakdown report after a repair in a hazardous area?
options: The team's opinion of the plant manager and operators
The cost of the team's lunch and travel for the day
A copy of last year's accounts for the whole company
The cause, the parts fitted with their Ex details and the tests

questions.stem: Before going to a breakdown in a classified area, why should you look up the equipment's marking and certificate details in the register?
options: So the team can choose matching uniforms for the job
So the correct certified spares can be taken to site
So the job can be priced higher than normal work
So the client is not able to complain about the bill

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: In the zone system, which zone number is used for a place where an explosive dust cloud is present all the time or for long periods?
What is the written document called that allows named, authorised people to do a stated job, with stated precautions, at a stated time?
Which gas group is used for the most easily ignited gases, such as hydrogen and acetylene?
Of the temperature classes T1 to T6, which one allows the lowest maximum surface temperature?
What instrument is used to check the air for flammable gas before and during work?
What is the name for the narrow gap between the machined faces of a flameproof joint, which cools any burning gas trying to escape?
On a gas detector, what do the letters LEL stand for?
What type of cable gland, filled with a setting compound, stops gas passing along inside the cable into a flameproof enclosure?
Which letter follows 'Ex' in the marking for intrinsic safety?
What kind of electric charge builds up when fuel flows through a hose or clothing rubs, and can make a spark?
What one word describes a liquid, such as petrol, whose vapour catches fire easily at normal air temperatures?
What two-word term is used for the lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off enough vapour to be lit by a flame?
Whose instructions set the type and tightening of the cover bolts on an Ex enclosure?
Which gas, the main part of natural gas and biogas, is found in sewage pumping stations and can form an explosive mixture with air?
What is the name (words or letters) of the bottled cooking gas used in Jamaica, which is heavier than air and collects in low places?

essays.stem: Explain what a hazardous area is. Describe the three gas zones and the three dust zones in general terms, and give a Jamaican workplace example where each kind of hazard may be found.
essays.modelAnswer: A hazardous area is a place where a flammable gas, vapour, mist or dust may be in the air in amounts that could be ignited, so electrical equipment there needs special protection and work needs special control. Sites are divided into zones on an area classification drawing. For gases and vapours, Zone 0 is where an explosive atmosphere is present all the time or for long periods, such as inside a fuel storage tank. Zone 1 is where it is likely now and then in normal operation, such as close to a fuel filling point. Zone 2 is where it is not likely in normal operation and would only last a short time, such as the wider area around pumps on a fuel station forecourt. Dusts use Zones 20, 21 and 22 in the same order. In Jamaica, gas and vapour hazards are found at fuel stations, LPG depots, distillery spirit stores and paint spray booths; dust hazards are found in sugar factories and flour or feed mills. The exact zones are always taken from the area classification drawing for the site.
markingPoints: Defines a hazardous area: flammable gas, vapour, mist or dust may be present
Zone 0, 1 and 2 explained in general terms
Dust zones 20, 21 and 22 named in the same order
Gives suitable Jamaican examples for gas or vapour and for dust
Says the zones come from the site's area classification drawing

essays.stem: Explain what information is found in the marking of electrical equipment for hazardous areas, and how you would check that a replacement item is suitable for the place where it will be fitted.
essays.modelAnswer: Equipment for hazardous areas carries an Ex marking that shows it has been certified. The marking states the type of protection, for example flameproof, increased safety or intrinsic safety. It shows the gas group (IIA, IIB or IIC, with IIC for the most easily ignited gases) or the dust group. It shows the temperature class, from T1 to T6, which limits how hot its surface may get, with T6 the coolest. It also has a certificate number, the maker's details and often an equipment protection level that links it to the zones it may be used in. To check a replacement, I would read the area classification drawing to find the zone, gas group and temperature class needed at that spot, then compare these with the marking on the replacement and its certificate. The protection type must suit the zone, the gas group must be the same or higher, and the temperature class must be the same or cooler. If anything does not match, or I am unsure, I would not fit it and would ask the authorised person.
markingPoints: Ex marking shows certified equipment and the type of protection
Gas group explained (IIC most demanding) and temperature class (T6 coolest)
Certificate number and maker's details; level of protection linked to zones
Compares the marking with what the area classification drawing requires
Does not fit it if it does not match; refers to the authorised person

essays.stem: A light fitting under a fuel station canopy has failed. The area classification drawing shows the spot as Zone 2. Describe the steps you would follow, from receiving the report to returning the light to service.
essays.modelAnswer: I would take the report and check the site register for the fitting's make, model and Ex marking, so I can bring a certified spare of the same type, gas group and temperature class. On site I would report to the person in charge and apply for a permit to work. The authorised person would arrange for the circuit to be isolated, locked and tagged, and the area tested with a bump-tested gas detector before and during the work, with the forecourt pumps near the work stopped if the permit says so. I would prove the circuit dead with a tester checked before and after use, and wait the time on the fitting's label before opening it. I would then find the cause, for example a failed lamp, driver or water inside, and replace the faulty part like for like. Before closing, I would check the joint faces, the seals, the glands and every bolt. The fitting would be inspected and the result recorded, the permit closed, and only then would the supply be restored by the authorised person. Finally I would update the register and write the report.
markingPoints: Checks the register and the marking; brings a matching certified spare
Permit to work; isolation, lock-off and gas testing arranged by the authorised person
Proves dead with a checked tester; waits the stated time before opening
Finds the cause and repairs like for like; checks joints, seals, glands and bolts
Inspection recorded, permit closed, supply restored by the authorised person, register updated

essays.stem: Compare flameproof (Ex d), increased safety (Ex e) and intrinsic safety (Ex i) protection. For each, say how it prevents an explosion and give one thing a technician must take care with during a repair.
essays.modelAnswer: A flameproof enclosure lets gas in but is strong enough to contain an explosion inside it. Any burning gas that escapes must pass through long, narrow joints called flamepaths, which cool it so it cannot light the gas outside. During a repair the technician must not damage, paint or add gaskets to the flamepath faces, and must refit every bolt of the right type. Increased safety equipment is designed so that arcs, sparks and hot spots do not happen in normal use, with good terminals, spacing and insulation. During a repair the technician must use the correct certified terminals, tighten them properly and fit no extra items inside. Intrinsic safety limits the voltage and current in the circuit so that even a fault cannot release enough energy to ignite the gas. During a repair the technician must keep IS wiring separate from other circuits, replace only like-for-like parts and never connect ordinary test gear that could add energy. In all three cases the equipment must be inspected and recorded before it goes back into service.
markingPoints: Flameproof: contains an internal explosion; flamepaths cool escaping gas
Flameproof care: no damage, paint or gaskets on flamepaths; all correct bolts
Increased safety: design prevents sparks and hot spots; correct terminals tightened
Intrinsic safety: energy limited so a fault cannot ignite gas; keep IS wiring separate
Like-for-like parts and inspection before return to service

essays.stem: Explain how a permit-to-work system controls breakdown work in a hazardous area, and why only authorised people may do this work.
essays.modelAnswer: A permit to work is a written system that makes sure dangerous work is planned, approved and controlled. Before a breakdown repair in a hazardous area, the person who issues the permit checks the job, the hazards and the zone. The permit lists the exact equipment and work, the electrical and process isolations, the gas tests and their results, the PPE, the tools allowed and the time it is valid. The person doing the work signs to say they understand it, and the work stays inside what is written. If conditions change, such as a gas alarm, work stops and the permit is suspended. When the work is finished, the permit is signed back, the equipment is inspected and the isolations are removed in a controlled way. Only authorised people may do the work because a hazardous area needs special knowledge: of zones, of protection types, of what must never be changed on certified equipment, and of the site's emergency plan. A mistake by an untrained person, such as a missing bolt or the wrong gland, can cause an explosion later.
markingPoints: Permit is a written system to plan, approve and control the work
Lists the equipment, isolations, gas tests, PPE and time limits
Worker signs; work stops and the permit is suspended if conditions change
Hand-back: inspection, removal of isolations, permit closed
Authorised people only, because special knowledge is needed and errors can cause explosions

essays.stem: Describe how gas testing should be carried out for breakdown work at an LPG depot, including the checks on the detector and where you would test.
essays.modelAnswer: Gas testing is done by a trained person, as the permit says. First the detector is checked: it must be the right type for the gas, within its calibration date, and bump-tested that day with a known test gas to prove the sensor and alarms work. Its battery must be charged for the length of the job. Testing is done before the permit is issued and then continuously or at set times during the work. LPG is heavier than air, so it collects in low places, so tests are taken near the ground, in pits, drains and trenches, and around the equipment to be worked on, not only at head height. If the gas were lighter than air, such as methane, tests would also be taken high up. Results are written on the permit with the time. Work starts only if the reading is at the safe level the permit sets, which is well below the lower explosive limit. If the alarm sounds at any time, work stops, the team leaves by the agreed route and the site emergency plan is followed.
markingPoints: Correct detector, in calibration, bump-tested the same day, charged
Test before work and continuously or at set times during it
LPG is heavier than air: test low, in pits and drains; lighter gases need high tests
Results recorded on the permit; work only at the safe level set
Alarm: stop, leave and follow the site emergency plan

essays.stem: Describe how you would inspect and close a flameproof enclosure after repairing a fault inside it, and explain why each check matters.
essays.modelAnswer: Before closing, I would check that nothing has been left inside, such as tools, off-cuts or loose screws, because they could cause a short circuit or a hot spot. I would inspect the flamepath faces on the cover and body for scratches, pitting or rust, because damage widens the gap and can let a flame escape. I would clean them only as the maker allows and never file them, paint them or add a gasket that the maker did not fit. Where the maker gives a maximum gap, it would be checked with feeler gauges. I would check that every cable gland is the correct certified type and properly tightened, and that any unused entry is closed with a certified stopping plug, because an open hole defeats the protection. I would refit every cover bolt, of the type the maker specifies, and tighten them evenly as the maker says, because a missing or loose bolt can let the joint open in an explosion. Finally, I would record the inspection and any parts used in the register and on the permit.
markingPoints: Nothing left inside the enclosure
Flamepath faces inspected; no filing, paint or extra gaskets; gap checked as the maker says
Correct certified glands, tight; unused entries closed with certified plugs
Every correct bolt fitted and tightened as the maker says
Inspection and parts recorded in the register and on the permit

essays.stem: Explain the sources of ignition a maintenance team could bring into a hazardous area during breakdown work, and how each one is controlled.
essays.modelAnswer: Electrical sparks can come from opening live equipment, from test instruments and from making or breaking connections. These are controlled by isolating and locking off, by proving dead with a tester the permit allows, and by using only certified instruments. Hot surfaces, such as a lamp just switched off or a hot motor, are controlled by waiting the time on the warning label before opening equipment. Hot work, such as welding, grinding and cutting, makes sparks and heat, so it needs a separate hot work permit, gas testing before and during the work, and fire cover. Static electricity can build up on people, hoses and plastic, so antistatic footwear and clothing are worn and metal parts are bonded to earth as the site says. Ordinary phones, radios, torches and cameras can spark, so only certified items are taken in. Tools that are dropped can strike sparks, so they are carried in pouches and tool use follows what the permit says. The team leader checks all of this at the briefing before entry.
markingPoints: Electrical sparks: isolation, lock-off, proving dead with permitted instruments
Hot surfaces: wait the stated cooling time
Hot work: separate permit, gas testing, fire cover
Static: antistatic footwear and clothing, bonding
Phones, torches and tools: certified items only; briefing by the team leader

essays.stem: During a breakdown at a distillery, the exact certified spare for a failed Ex motor is not in stock and production is losing money. Explain what you would do and why you must not fit a non-matching item.
essays.modelAnswer: I would tell the person in charge straight away that the exact spare is not available and explain the choices. A replacement must have the right protection type for the zone, a gas group the same or higher and a temperature class the same or cooler than the area classification drawing requires, and it must be certified. I would check whether another certified motor in stores, or one from the supplier, meets all of these and the duty of the pump, and have the authorised person approve it. If there is none, the equipment must stay isolated and out of service, and a safe temporary plan agreed, such as a standby pump or a pause in that part of the process. I must not fit an ordinary motor or one with the wrong marking, because a normal motor can make sparks or hot spots that can ignite the alcohol vapour, causing an explosion or fire that could kill people and destroy the plant. Losing production is a cost, but it can be recovered; an explosion cannot. I would record the decision and order the correct spare.
markingPoints: Informs the person in charge and explains the options
Any substitute must be certified with suitable protection, gas group and temperature class
Authorised person approves; otherwise the equipment stays isolated
Explains the danger: sparks or hot surfaces can ignite the vapour
Agrees a safe temporary plan, records the decision and orders the correct spare

essays.stem: As the team leader for a breakdown repair in a hazardous area, explain how you would brief and supervise your team, and what records you would complete at the end.
essays.modelAnswer: Before entry I would hold a short briefing at the permit point. I would explain the job, the zone and the hazards from the area classification drawing, the conditions on the permit, the isolations in place, the gas test results and who is testing, the PPE, the tools and items allowed, and the emergency plan, including the escape route and the meeting point. I would check that every member is trained and authorised for the area, and keep anyone who is not outside it. I would give each person a clear task. During the work I would stay with the team, watch that nobody goes beyond the permit, check the gas readings, and stop the work if anything changes. At the end I would check the equipment myself before it is closed and make sure the inspection is done and recorded. I would sign the permit back, report to the authorised person, and complete the breakdown report: the fault, the cause, the parts fitted with their Ex details, the tests and the time out of service. I would also update the equipment register.
markingPoints: Briefing covers the job, zone, permit conditions, isolations, gas tests, PPE and emergency plan
Checks everyone is trained and authorised; gives clear tasks
Supervises throughout and stops work if conditions change
Checks and records the inspection; signs back the permit
Completes the breakdown report and updates the register

practical1.title: Plan the response to a pump motor breakdown at a fuel depot (paper exercise)
practical1.brief: This is a planning exercise done at the Centre on paper. Nobody enters a real hazardous area. The assessor gives the group a site sketch with an area classification drawing extract, the motor's nameplate and Ex marking details, and a short report: 'Pump P2 at the loading bay has tripped and will not restart.' As a group, prepare a full breakdown response pack. Share the roles: the team leader writes the method statement and runs a five-minute briefing at the end; one member completes the permit-to-work request; one prepares the isolation plan (electrical and process) and the gas testing plan; one checks the marking against the zone and writes the spares and tools list; one writes the risk assessment and the emergency plan. Each member presents their part during the briefing, and the group checks each other's work. Photograph each document and the briefing.
materials: Site sketch with an area classification drawing extract (supplied by the assessor)
Motor nameplate and Ex marking details (supplied by the assessor)
Blank permit-to-work request, risk assessment and method statement forms
Isolation plan and gas test record forms
Flip-chart paper, markers, rulers and pens
photos: The isolation plan and the gas testing plan
The spares list, showing the marking checked against the zone, gas group and temperature class
The risk assessment and emergency plan
The team leader's briefing, with each member presenting their part
checklist: Read the zone, gas group and temperature class correctly from the drawing extract
Completed their own document clearly and accurately
Included both electrical and process isolation, with lock-off and proving dead
Planned gas testing before and during work with a bump-tested detector
Chose only certified spares that match the marking needed
Stated that only authorised people do the work under the permit
Included an emergency plan with an escape route and meeting point
Presented their part clearly and answered the assessor's questions
safety: This is a classroom exercise: no member enters or works in a real hazardous area
Plans must keep all live and hot work under the control of authorised people
Use only the information given by the assessor; do not guess figures for a real site
Keep the classroom tidy and walkways clear of bags and paper

practical2.title: Inspect, repair and close an Ex-type enclosure on a dead training rig
practical2.brief: As a group, carry out a simulated breakdown repair on the Centre's training enclosure (an Ex-type junction box or light fitting kept for training and never connected to a supply, or a standard enclosure the assessor uses as a stand-in). The assessor issues a training permit and has planted faults, such as a damaged lamp, a wrong gland, a missing bolt and an open entry. First the group isolates the training board that 'feeds' the rig, applies a group lock-off and proves it dead with a tester checked before and after. The team leader then reads out the permit and the waiting time on the label. Members take turns to open the enclosure, inspect the flamepath faces and record their condition, check gaps with feeler gauges against the figure the assessor gives, replace the faulty parts like for like from the spares tray, fit a stopping plug in any unused entry, and refit and tighten every bolt as the maker's sheet says. The group completes an inspection checklist, a breakdown report and a register update, and hands the permit back. Every member does at least one repair step and signs for it. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Training Ex-type enclosure or stand-in enclosure, never connected to a supply
Training board with lockable isolator, group lock box, padlocks and tags
Feeler gauges and the maker's data sheet for the enclosure
Spares tray: lamp, certified-type gland, stopping plug, cover bolts (with wrong items mixed in)
Torque screwdriver or wrench, hand tools
Training permit, inspection checklist, breakdown report and register forms
photos: Group lock-off applied, with every member's padlock and tag
The tester being proved before and after the dead test
The opened enclosure with the planted faults found and marked
Feeler gauge check on the flamepath, with the record sheet
Correct spares fitted, and the stopping plug in the unused entry
The closed enclosure with every bolt fitted, and the signed checklist and report
checklist: Applied their own lock and tag and took part in proving dead
Waited the stated time before opening, as the permit and label said
Inspected the flamepath and recorded its condition without damaging it
Chose the correct certified-type parts and rejected the wrong items
Fitted a stopping plug in the unused entry
Fitted every bolt of the right type and tightened it as the maker's sheet says
Completed and signed their part of the inspection checklist and report
Removed their lock only when the work was finished and checked
safety: The rig is never connected to a supply; only the instructor may energise anything at the Centre
Treat the rig as if it were live until proved dead, and keep the group lock-off on throughout
Do not file, paint or grease flamepath faces; handle machined parts carefully
Use the correct tools and do not over-tighten bolts beyond the maker's figure
